questions.question: Why give each feature folder an index.ts public API?
options: Bundlers require an index file in every folder
It makes every file in the feature importable from anywhere
Other code imports only the stable surface, so the owning team can refactor internals freely
It disables tree-shaking for that feature
questions.explanation: A public API hides internal files. Combined with lint rules against deep imports, it keeps features decoupled.

questions.question: In a Module Federation setup, why should react and react-dom be shared as singletons?
options: Two copies of React on one page break hooks and Context
It makes each remote load faster than a monolith
It lets each remote use a different major React version
questions.explanation: Hooks and Context rely on a single React instance. Duplicate copies cause invalid hook call errors and missing context values.

questions.question: What is the main reason to adopt micro-frontends?
options: They always reduce total JavaScript payload
They remove the need for a design system
Separate teams need to build and deploy parts of the UI independently
questions.explanation: Micro-frontends are an organisational scaling tool. They usually add payload, version skew and integration risk.

questions.question: Which dependency direction is healthy in a feature-based structure?
options: app/ uses features/, and both use shared/, with no feature-to-feature deep imports
Every feature imports every other feature's internals
questions.explanation: Dependencies should flow one way toward shared/. shared/ must stay free of feature knowledge, and cycles between features signal misplaced code.
